user.title: Connect to the Vördr hub
user.description: Home Assistant becomes a client of the hub. It creates its own key; the hub's operator admits it.

data_description.url: WebSocket address of the hub, e.g. wss://hub.example:8443/v1/ha
data_description.name: How this Home Assistant appears at the hub: lower case letters, digits, dot and hyphen
data_description.ca_pem: Only if the hub's certificate comes from an own CA; then only this CA is trusted

progress.approval:
Waiting for the hub's operator. Compare the fingerprint and admit this client on the hub:

`{command}`

Fingerprint: `{fingerprint}`

error.invalid_name: Use lower case letters, digits, dot and hyphen (at most 63 characters).
error.probe_dns: The hub's name does not resolve.
error.probe_connect: No connection to the hub (address, port, firewall, hub not running).
error.probe_tls: The hub's certificate is not trusted (chain, name or CA certificate).
error.probe_websocket: TLS works, but there is no Vördr endpoint at this path.
error.probe_challenge: The other side answers, but it is no Vördr hub speaking this protocol.

abort.already_configured: This hub is already set up.
abort.unreachable: The hub could not be reached while waiting for approval.
abort.approval_timeout: No decision within an hour. Start again; the hub keeps the request.
abort.rejected_key_mismatch: The hub knows this client name with another key. Choose another name or forget the client on the hub (vordr-hub forget-client).
abort.rejected_too_many_pending: Too many clients are waiting for approval at the hub.
abort.rejected_rejected: The operator rejected this client at the hub.
abort.rejected_protocol_mismatch: The hub speaks another protocol version than this integration; update one of them.
abort.rejected_bad_hello: The hub did not accept the login (invalid name or signature).

state.rejected_not_allowed: Rejected: not allowed by the host
state.precheck_vetting_unavailable: Hub could not check the plan
state.failed_target_hostkey: Device SSH host key does not match

state.offline: Check the host and its agent
state.stale: Install the updates, by hand or with the button
state.malicious_package: Remove the package and treat the host as compromised
state.vulnerable_package: Update the package to a fixed version
state.ok_reboot_required: Reboot within the window or with the button
state.rejected_invalid_job: Check the hub and the clock – this may point to an attack
state.rejected_outside_window: Wait for the maintenance window, or start it outside the window with a reason (action “Install outside the window” or “Run outside the window”)
state.rejected_busy: Try again later; stop other updaters running at the same time (e.g. unattended-upgrades)
state.precheck_repo_unreachable: Check the package source and the network
state.precheck_would_remove_packages: Decide by hand: the update would remove packages
state.precheck_version_flagged: Look at the OSV entry and wait for a fixed version
state.precheck_version_too_new: Wait until the release is old enough
state.precheck_not_from_registry: Look at where the dependency points; update such a location by hand
state.failed_package_manager: Read the excerpt of the last run
state.failed_verification: Read the excerpt of the last run
state.failed_health: Look at the service named in the run
state.failed_target_auth: Check the device's service account and its password in the secret store
state.failed_target_tls: Check the device's certificate; if it changed on purpose, update the pinned fingerprint - otherwise someone may be in between
state.failed_target_hostkey: Check the device's SSH host key (ssh-keyscan); if it changed on purpose, update target.host_key - otherwise someone may be in between
state.failed_config_backup: Look at the proxy instance's log; without a fresh backup no firmware update starts
state.failed_backup: Read the run's detail and the hypervisor's backup log; nothing was installed
state.aborted: Start the run again if needed
state.unknown: Bring agent and hub to the same version
state.reboot_pending_manual: Reboot by hand - this host does not allow reboots through Vördr

command_refused.message: {node}: the hub did not run the command ({code}).

refresh_dependencies_unsupported.message: {node}: the dependencies of {location} cannot be refreshed (so far only npm folders with a lock file, and an agent from 0.12.0 on).

update_image_not_allowed.message: {node}: {service} cannot be updated by button. The host's agent.yaml must allow it (image:{service} in install.allowed_scopes), and its image must carry a tag without a pinned digest and come from a registry.

command_refused_role_forbids.message: {node}: this Home Assistant may not start that - its role at the hub does not allow it (vordr-hub client-role).

command_refused_backup_stale.message: {node}: not installed - the last backup ({group}) is {age} h old, at most {max} h are allowed. Back up first, then install.

command_refused_backup_missing.message: {node}: not installed - PBS has no backup in {group}.

command_refused_backup_unreachable.message: {node}: not installed - Proxmox Backup Server does not answer, so the backup cannot be checked.

command_refused_backup_unmapped.message: {node}: not installed - hub.yaml names no PBS group for this host (backup.guests).

command_refused_backup_host_unavailable.message: {node}: not installed - the backup before the install is made by {hypervisor}, and its agent is not there (offline, not approved, or without guest_backup).

outside_window_unsupported.message: {node}: runs outside the window need a newer hub and agent. Update them first; until then the window holds.

outside_window_no_window.message: {node}: this has no window - use the normal button, it works at any time.

command_refused_outside_window.message: {node}: not installed - the host's window is closed, and its agent is too old to install outside it. Update the agent, or wait for the window.

command_refused_rate_limited.message: {node}: not installed - its last run was less than its minimum interval (install.min_interval_h) ago. Possible again from {next}.

confirm.title: Reboot {node} now?
confirm.description: Updates on {node} take full effect only after a reboot. Vördr asks the hub for the same reboot as the host's reboot button: the agent reboots only if it is still needed, and the host reports back once it is up again.

abort.hub_not_connected: Home Assistant is not connected to the Vördr hub right now. Try again once it is.
abort.reboot_not_offered: {node} no longer allows reboots through Vördr. Reboot it by hand.
abort.command_refused: The hub refused the reboot of {node} (code {code}).

reboot_required_manual.title: Vördr: {node} needs a reboot
reboot_required_manual.description: {node} has needed a reboot since {since}. This host does not allow reboots through Vördr: reboot it by hand. This notice goes away by itself once the host no longer needs a reboot.

update_package.name: Update a package
update_package.description: Updates one pip or npm package of a location to its candidate (public for at least the host's minimum age, checked against OSV by the hub).

package.name: Package
package.description: Name of the package, as the location lists it.

reason.name: Reason (outside the window)
reason.description: Optional: why now, outside the host's maintenance window. Without one, the hub notes that it was started in Home Assistant. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.

refresh_dependencies.name: Refresh dependencies
refresh_dependencies.description: Moves the dependencies of a location that have findings to the newest release their dependents allow (public for at least the host's minimum age, checked against OSV by the hub). A dependency that no allowed release fixes stays as it is; the run says why.

reason.name: Reason (outside the window)
reason.description: Optional: why now, outside the host's maintenance window. Without one, the hub notes that it was started in Home Assistant. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.

install_outside_window.name: Install outside the window
install_outside_window.description: Installs like the install button of a Vördr update entity (system packages, a pip/npm location or container images), with a reason of your own. The install button itself also runs outside the host's maintenance window; this action says why. Automatic runs keep to the window.

reason.name: Reason
reason.description: Why now, at most 200 bytes. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.

press_outside_window.name: Run outside the window
press_outside_window.description: Presses a Vördr button (install security updates, install an app, reboot) with a reason of your own. A reboot outside the host's window needs it; the install buttons run outside the window anyway. Rebooting still needs the admin role at the hub.

reason.name: Reason
reason.description: Why now, at most 200 bytes. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.

update_image.name: Update a container image
update_image.description: Moves one Compose service to the rebuild of its tag, once that build is at least the host's minimum age old. The running image stays on the host as the way back: if the service does not come back healthy, the agent returns to it. A newer tag needs the Compose file changed and stays manual.

service.name: Service
service.description: The Compose service as <project>/<service>, as the entity's attribute updates lists it under services.

reason.name: Reason (outside the window)
reason.description: Optional: why now, outside the host's maintenance window. Without one, the hub notes that it was started in Home Assistant. Stays with the run, in the agent log and in the hub's event log.
